Kimberly — quick tax ops read: the VIES failure is almost certainly a formatting/normalisation issue (space + trailing letter). VIES will sometimes reject IDs with extraneous spacing or older suffixes. However, the attached certificate does show the VAT number and legal name match and includes the registration issue date.

Suggested path (compliant, pragmatic):
1) Accept the attached VAT certificate as supporting evidence for B2B reverse-charge (per our policy) provided the certificate is dated and displays the registration number clearly.
2) Issue credit note CN-202605-ACRO for the gross VAT amount (reverse the original VAT charge).
3) Issue new invoice INV-202605-RC with net amounts and a prominent note: "Reverse-charge: recipient liable for VAT. AcroSoft Ltd. VAT: IE1234567A".
4) Record the validation event in our tax log (I’ll attach a short checklog).

We should also request a signed copy of the VAT certificate (company-stamped or signed by an authorised representative) for audit trail — that satisfies finance and auditors. Once steps 1-3 are done, payments can be released against INV-202605-RC. If AcroSoft requires us to reissue with their legal entity line exactly as on certificate, do that — ask them to confirm the exact legal name string.

I’ve generated a validation checklist and stub log: validation_checklog.txt (attached). Estimated time to create CN + new invoice: same day if payments team confirms.

Ben Carter
